record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; the full research document and experiment files were not provided or read.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal outcomes after a direction-based weight edit on released models, testing practical removal with a different intervention from activation ablation.
record.gate_note: The README gives post-edit refusal counts and rates, plus a dense-only versus EGA comparison for the 26B-A4B model. It reports KL values but no task-based capability results; a sanity-check script is listed without results. The README describes directions computed from harmful and harmless prompts, but does not report activation ablation or adding a direction.
record.test_reason: The repo applies direction-based weight edits (abliteration) to released Gemma 4 instruct models, including a MoE and a 'Unified' architecture, and reports post-edit refusal rates on harmful-prompt benchmarks. That bears on V2 in a new model family and architecture. The method is a norm-preserving biprojection variant, not the original recipe.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say biprojection, plus EGA for MoE, removes refusal across dense, MoE and Unified Gemma 4 models. They also say larger models absorb abliteration better (lower KL), MoE experts carry most of the refusal signal, and the Unified model needs only its upper layers ablated. Their claim of a 'sub-1%' refusal rate for all models is contradicted by their own table (12B 2.0%, 31B 3.2%).
record.recipe_differences: The original claim concerns projecting a difference-in-means direction out of residual activations at every layer and position, and adding it. This repo computes per-layer directions from 800 harmful and harmless prompt residuals, orthogonalizes against harmless means, and projects directions out of model weights; it uses EGA for MoE models. Repo type: tool/research repo; the README says it is built on heretic and does not claim to reproduce the original study.
record.method_sensitivity: For the 12B Unified model, only the top 70% of layers (L15-47) are abliterated; the README says the refusal signal sits in the upper layers. For the MoE model, dense-only abliteration leaves 29/100 refusals, while adding EGA leaves 3/100.

fits_no_version.finding: Task vector negation for removing refusal shows a sharp phase transition with no usable middle ground.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal removal by task-vector negation is not graded; it switches abruptly.

fits_no_version.finding: Directions computed under 4-bit quantization match bf16 directions (mean cosine 0.935).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction is robust to quantization of the model used to compute it.

record.problems: No untreated refusal rates are given for the released-model results. The README reports no task-based capability evaluation results; the listed sanity-check script is not itself evidence of such a check. The reported refusal rates are post-edit outcomes, and the README notes most flagged refusals were refusal-then-comply false positives.
record.rows_left_out: KL divergence values are listed in the Models table but are not task-based measures of general capability or refusal, so they are not included as claim-outcome rows. No other row results are reported in the supplied README.

untested.parts: Preservation of general capabilities: only KL divergence is reported, and sanity_check.py results are not shown. The untreated refusal rate is not reported.
Activation ablation, direction addition and capability retention are not reported.
Not tested. Per-layer directions and expert-level edits are used, but single versus multi-direction structure is not compared.
Not tested; directions are computed separately for each model.

missing.what: Untreated (pre-edit) refusal rates for each Gemma 4 model
Baseline versus abliterated quality comparison from sanity_check.py
12B result when all layers (100%) are abliterated, the comparison behind the 70% choice
KL divergence per model (0.056-0.346), a proxy for distribution shift that varies with model size

record.verdict_notes: Only the README was read. The 29/100 and 3/100 results come from a 100-prompt set, a different set from the 686-prompt evaluation. The authors note that default refusal-marker matching is unreliable and that flagged refusals were audited by hand. This is a community repo, not peer reviewed, built on heretic.

versions.untested_parts: No activation projection-out or direction addition results, and no reported test of general capabilities.
No untreated refusal-rate baseline is reported for the released-model table.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
Per-layer directions and expert-level edits are described, but the README does not test whether refusal is better described by multiple directions, a cone, or an affine structure.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
The method is applied separately to model variants; transfer of a direction between variants, languages, or base and instruct models is not tested.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages.
